LLAMA_PORT.description: Host port llama-server binds on. Since #1416 this is the ROUTER port: one llama-server process serves four presets here — `gemma-4-e4b` (the household model), `gemma-4-12b` (foundry, 131072 with q8 KV), `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` (reading and thinking, 131072 with q8 KV) and `qwen3.8-27b` (coding, 81920) — and a client picks one with the `model` field of its request; `GET /v1/models` lists them. Only one is resident at a time (`--models-max 1`), and asking for another evicts it and loads the new one in 9-19 s. The router has no policy of its own: which presets are allowed is decided one layer up, by the GPU lease mode, and enforced by the Solaris Engine. Default `11435` — next to Ollama's 11434 and clear of llama.cpp's stock 8080, which is heavily contended on a household box. Keep it equal to the solaris template's LLAMA_SERVER_URL port. There is deliberately no proxy route: llama-server ships no authentication, so the endpoint is for on-box consumers only. It binds every host interface rather than loopback because isolated pods (claude-dev's `pi`) reach it via host.containers.internal, which rootless podman/pasta maps to the host's LAN address rather than loopback (ADR 0007, Decision 3). LAN devices are refused at the HOST firewall by the blockLanAccess flag below: ServiceBay installs an nftables rule that drops connections arriving on a physical interface while leaving loopback — and the pasta-proxied pod path, which lands on lo — untouched.

LLAMA_MODEL_REPO.description: Hugging Face repo the GGUFs are downloaded from at install. Default `ggml-org/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF` — ggml's own conversion of `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, and the only source that also ships the matching MTP drafter. Ollama's own e4b blob cannot be used: llama.cpp rejects it (`expected 2131 tensors, got 720`), which is why this template downloads its own weights instead of pointing at the ollama model store.

LLAMA_MODEL_FILE.description: The chat weights, downloaded into ${DATA_DIR}/llama/models. Default `gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_0.gguf` (4.59 GB) — the household model, box-measured at 133.5 tok/s and 0.30 s per finished answer with the drafter below, against 53.0 tok/s / 0.62 s for the same model on Ollama (solarisbay#1318). Gemma 4 12B was measured too and rejected: 1.35 s per answer, more than twice the wait for the resident.

LLAMA_MODEL_ALIAS.description: The name of the household preset: the section name in `presets.ini`, what `GET /v1/models` lists, what a client puts in the `model` field to be answered by Gemma 4 E4B, and what llama-server reports back in its /v1 answers (`--alias`). Default `gemma-4-e4b`. The other three presets are named by the template itself: `gemma-4-12b`, `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` and `qwen3.8-27b` (solarisbay#1333, #1416).

LLAMA_DRAFT_FILE.description: Google's official Multi-Token-Prediction drafter for the same model (98.7 MB), the whole reason this template exists — speculative decoding roughly doubles the household answer rate and Ollama has no draft-model knob at all. Set to an empty string only to measure without it; the server then runs at about half the speed.

LLAMA_MMPROJ_FILE.description: The multimodal projector (560 MB) that keeps Gemma 4's vision working, so photo attachments in the chat are still understood after the move off Ollama. Blank disables it: the server starts text-only and an attached photo reaches the model as text alone. Costs about 0.5 GB of VRAM.

LLAMA_EMBED_PORT.description: Host loopback port the embeddings server binds on. Default `11436` — next to the chat server's 11435. This second llama-server instance runs `nomic-embed-text` with `--embeddings` and serves OpenAI `/v1/embeddings`; it replaces Ollama, which used to be the only reason that service was still installed (solarisbay#1332). It costs about 300 MB of VRAM and binds 127.0.0.1 only: its one consumer is the Solaris Engine, which shares this host's network namespace. Set to an empty string to skip the embeddings server entirely — the vault's semantic search then degrades to keyword search.

LLAMA_EMBED_REPO.description: Hugging Face repo the embedding GGUF is downloaded from. Default `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-GGUF` — nomic's own conversion of the model Ollama served under the tag `nomic-embed-text`, so vectors already in `okf_vectors` stay comparable with newly computed ones.

LLAMA_EMBED_FILE.description: The embedding weights. Default `nomic-embed-text-v1.5.f16.gguf` (274 MB) — the same quantisation Ollama's `nomic-embed-text` tag ships, deliberately: a smaller quant would move the vectors away from the ~46k already stored and semantic search would silently get worse. 768 dimensions, mean pooling, no query/document prefix — exactly what the Ollama path produced.

LLAMA_EMBED_ALIAS.description: The name the embeddings server reports in the `model` field of its answers, and the name written into the `okf_vectors.model` column. Default `nomic-embed-text` — the tag the Ollama era used, kept so old and new rows read the same.

LLAMA_EMBED_CONTEXT_LENGTH.description: Context window of the embeddings server (tokens). Default `2048` — nomic-embed-text v1.5's native window, and what Ollama loaded it at. The batch size is pinned to the same value: an embedding model runs non-causal attention, so llama.cpp requires a micro-batch at least as large as the window or it refuses the request.

LLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH.description: Context window the HOUSEHOLD preset is loaded at (tokens). Default `32768` — the same window the household prompt was measured against (7.7k of system prompt, tools and entity registry, leaving ~25k of conversation), and what the chat's auto-compaction assumes; the operator's ruling of 2026-09-13 is that e4b stays at 32k. The other three presets carry their own window in `presets.ini` (131072 for the 12B and the 35B-A3B, 81920 for the 27B). Unlike Ollama this is a per-preset setting, not a per-request hint: raising it costs KV-cache VRAM on every turn.

LLAMA_DRAFT_N_MAX.description: How many tokens the MTP drafter proposes per step for the household preset (`--spec-draft-n-max`). Default `4`: box-measured 43.4% of drafted tokens accepted at 4, against 25% at 8 — on Gemma a longer draft wastes more GPU work than it saves. The coding preset runs `8` instead, where the drafter is accepted 75% of the time and the longer draft buys 17% (solarisbay#1415). Only change this with a measurement in hand.

LLAMA_GPU_PASSTHROUGH.description: Blank = auto-detect: post-deploy engages NVIDIA GPU passthrough when the host has a CDI-registered GPU (`/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml`, from `nvidia-ctk cdi generate`), otherwise CPU-only. `yes` forces GPU, `no` forces CPU. Actual passthrough is delivered by post-deploy's Quadlet fixup, which swaps the .kube unit for a `.container` with `AddDevice=nvidia.com/gpu=all` AND `SecurityLabelDisable=true`. Both lines are load-bearing: with the device but without the SELinux relaxation, llama-server logs a single passing warning and quietly answers from the CPU.

LLAMA_DOWNLOAD_STALL_SECONDS.description: Stall window for the GGUF downloads, in seconds: a download is abandoned only after this long with NO bytes arriving — not on total elapsed time, so a slow link taking half an hour for the 4.6 GB weights is fine as long as it keeps moving. Also caps the wait for llama-server to answer /health (at most 900 s, since the first start loads ~5 GB from disk).
